title: Founding of Liliw by Gat Tayaw
description: Gat Tayaw and his followers establish the upland settlement at the foot of Mt. Banahaw. According to local lore, a bird alighted atop a ceremonial bamboo pole and sang 'Liw, Liw, Liw,' giving birth to the name Liliw.

title: Establishment of the Franciscan Parish
description: Franciscan missionaries establish the independent parish of St. John the Baptist and begin constructing Liliw's iconic baroque red-brick church.

title: Philippine Revolution and First Republic
description: Liliweños join the revolutionary movement in Laguna against Spanish colonial rule and establish local municipal governance under the First Philippine Republic.

title: Standardization of the Name 'Lilio'
description: During the American civil administration, the town's official spelling is standardized to 'Lilio' for postal and administrative records.

title: Liberation of Liliw
description: Combined Filipino guerilla units and Allied forces liberate Liliw from Japanese occupation toward the end of World War II, preserving its historic church and town center.

title: Restoration of the Official Name 'Liliw'
description: By virtue of Republic Act No. 4346 enacted on June 19, 1965, the municipality officially restores its traditional indigenous name 'Liliw' in place of 'Lilio'.

title: First Gat Tayaw Tsinelas Festival
description: Liliw launches the annual Gat Tayaw Tsinelas Festival every April to celebrate its thriving footwear industry and cement its identity as the 'Tsinelas Capital of Laguna'.

title: Highland Agro-Eco Tourism & Civic Tech
description: Liliw expands its highland cold-spring resorts, heritage tourism along Gat Tayaw Street, and community-driven digital transparency initiatives through BetterLiliw.
